claim: Kindiki was among the Cabinet Secretaries dismissed when President Ruto dissolved the entire Cabinet on 11 July 2024 (no allegations cited), and was among six ex-CSs re-nominated to the new Cabinet.
quote: Six out of the 11 Cabinet Secretaries who survived the axe following the dismissal of the Cabinet by President William Ruto will be vetted afresh... They include Kindiki Kithure (Interior), Aden Duale (Defence), Alice Wahome (Lands), Soipan Tuya (Environment), Davis Chirchir (Transport), and Rebecca Miano (Attorney General), who were nominated back to Cabinet as President Ruto reconstitutes his government.
legal_status: dismissed from prior office (no allegations cited - Speaker: 'There are no allegations against them'); re-nominated

claim: At his 1 August 2024 vetting, Kindiki was questioned about his silence during the June-July 2024 anti-government protests during which protesters were abducted and killed, and replied that the events were 'operational issues' outside his remit.
quote: Kindiki was responding to a query from Suna East MP Junet Mohamed who questioned why the CS remained silent during the Gen Z protests at a time when protestors were abducted and killed. "The reason that I didn't talk everyday is because the events were mainly operational issues."
legal_status: questioned at vetting; no criminal charge

claim: Kindiki himself recited at vetting the toll of deaths, injuries and arrests that occurred under the National Police Service while he was the Interior minister responsible for it.
quote: It is unfortunate that during recent protests, we witnessed the deaths of 42 Kenyans, 486 civilians and 285 police injured. We had about 1,387 arrests, 54 police cars destroyed and 110 vehicles also destroyed, therefore I want to say the operational responsibility lies within the National Police Service.
legal_status: self-admitted figures stated by the nominee at vetting (context of accountability questioning)

claim: Wahome served as Lands CS in the Cabinet dismissed on 11 July 2024 and was re-nominated to the same docket.
quote: They include Kindiki Kithure (Interior), Aden Duale (Defence), Alice Wahome (Lands), Soipan Tuya (Environment), Davis Chirchir (Transport), and Rebecca Miano (Attorney General), who were nominated back to Cabinet as President Ruto reconstitutes his government.
legal_status: dismissed from prior office (no allegations cited); re-nominated

claim: During her vetting, Wahome struggled to explain her ministry's relationship with the National Land Commission, a live institutional dispute in Kenyan land governance.
quote: Lands Cabinet Secretary nominee Alice Wahome had a hard time explaining her office's relationship with the National Land Commission when she appeared for vetting Thursday.
legal_status: questioned at vetting (governance/suitability issue; no allegation of personal wrongdoing reported)

claim: Tuya served as Environment CS in the Cabinet dismissed on 11 July 2024, was re-nominated, and had her proposed docket switched from Environment to Defence in the re-shuffle.
quote: They include Kindiki Kithure (Interior), Aden Duale (Defence), Alice Wahome (Lands), Soipan Tuya (Environment), Davis Chirchir (Transport), and Rebecca Miano (Attorney General), who were nominated back to Cabinet as President Ruto reconstitutes his government.
legal_status: dismissed from prior office (no allegations cited); re-nominated to a different docket

claim: After his nomination, Karanja faced a public claim that he had been personal assistant to sacked Agriculture CS Mithika Linturi, which he denied at vetting.
quote: "This one caught me by surprise. For the record Mr Speaker sir and honourable members, I have never met the former minister for Agriculture and I have never been a personal assistant," Karanja said. After his nomination by President Ruto, it was alleged that Karanja was the PA to Linturi.
legal_status: public allegation, denied by nominee on the record at vetting

claim: Duale served as Defence CS in the Cabinet dismissed on 11 July 2024 and was re-nominated, his proposed docket moving between Defence and Environment.
quote: They include Kindiki Kithure (Interior), Aden Duale (Defence), Alice Wahome (Lands), Soipan Tuya (Environment), Davis Chirchir (Transport), and Rebecca Miano (Attorney General), who were nominated back to Cabinet as President Ruto reconstitutes his government.
legal_status: dismissed from prior office (no allegations cited); re-nominated

claim: Parliament's own analysis of the public-participation memoranda recorded 69 objections against Duale's nomination, among the highest of any of the 20 vetted nominees.
quote: According to an analysis done by Parliament and seen by Nation, Mr Murkomen received 92 petitions, Joho 72, and Duale 69 memorandums.
legal_status: documented public objections to appointment (content of objections not adjudicated)

claim: In 2018, as Majority Leader, Duale argued against a blanket DCI/EACC investigation of all MPs into the 'toilet bribery' scandal that led to the rejection of the contraband-sugar report - an episode raised repeatedly against him as a leadership-integrity question.
quote: "This is a serious matter Mr Speaker, allowing other agencies to investigate members can drag to 2022 and some MPs might not be cleared to vie for elections. Let the people who made the allegations go to DCI and EACC as ordinary Kenyans and give evidence, but you cannot indict 349 MPs, including the Speaker, with no evidence," he stated.
legal_status: self-admitted statements on the record; Duale himself was not among the MPs named as having received bribes in that report

claim: Chirchir served as Transport CS in the Cabinet dismissed on 11 July 2024 and was re-nominated to the Roads docket.
quote: They include Kindiki Kithure (Interior), Aden Duale (Defence), Alice Wahome (Lands), Soipan Tuya (Environment), Davis Chirchir (Transport), and Rebecca Miano (Attorney General), who were nominated back to Cabinet as President Ruto reconstitutes his government.
legal_status: dismissed from prior office (no allegations cited); re-nominated

claim: Parliament's analysis recorded 58 public petitions challenging Chirchir's nomination as Roads CS.
quote: According to the document, Interior CS nominee Kithure Kindiki received 68 petitions, while David Chirchir, who has been nominated as Roads CS, received 58 petitions
legal_status: documented public objections to appointment

claim: Mvurya, Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs CS from November 2022, was in the Cabinet dismissed in July 2024; he formally handed the Mining docket to Hassan Joho on 9 August 2024 and was retained instead for Investments, Trade and Industry.
quote: Joho assumed office on August 9, succeeding Salim Mvurya, in a ceremony overseen by President William Ruto.
legal_status: prior office ended via collective Cabinet dismissal (no allegations cited); re-appointed to a different docket

claim: Miano accepted nomination as the first female Attorney General on 19 July 2024 but was withdrawn from that nomination days later; she asked to be 'assigned lighter duties' and was instead nominated to Tourism and Wildlife.
quote: Miano, previously the Cabinet Secretary for Investments and Trade, had been reassigned to the role of Attorney General in new Cabinet nominations announced by Ruto last week. She had accepted the nomination and expressed gratitude for the opportunity on her X account on July 19, 2024.
legal_status: self-admitted acceptance then withdrawal from AG nomination (no wrongdoing alleged)

claim: Ruto's amended 24 July 2024 list dropped Miano from the Attorney-General nomination and retained her for Tourism and Wildlife.
quote: President Ruto retained Cabinet Secretaries Salim Mvurya (Investments, Trade and Industry) and Rebecca Miano in Tourism and Wildlife after an amended list dropped her from the Attorney-General nomination
legal_status: nomination changed by appointing authority (no wrongdoing alleged)

claim: At his 3-4 August 2024 vetting, Wandayi was pressed by MPs on how he would pivot from a decade as a vocal ODM opposition MP to implementing President Ruto's programme.
quote: Energy and Petroleum Cabinet Secretary nominee Opiyo Wandayi found himself in a tight corner during his vetting as he was taken to task over how he will shift from his role of opposition to implementing government policies.
legal_status: questioned at vetting (suitability/political-consistency issue; no allegation of wrongdoing reported)

claim: Murkomen, Roads and Transport CS in the post-2022 Cabinet, was dismissed in the 11 July 2024 dissolution and re-nominated a fortnight later, moving from Roads to Youth Affairs, Creative Economy and Sports.
quote: Former Cabinet Secretaries Kipchumba Murkomen, who managed the Roads docket, and Moses Kuria, who oversaw Performance and Service Delivery, were among the outspoken members dismissed by President Ruto.
legal_status: dismissed from prior office (no allegations cited); re-nominated to a different docket

claim: Parliament's analysis recorded 92 public petitions against Murkomen's nomination - the highest of any of the 20 vetted nominees.
quote: According to an analysis done by Parliament and seen by Nation, Mr Murkomen received 92 petitions, Joho 72, and Duale 69 memorandums.
legal_status: documented public objections to appointment (highest of any nominee)

claim: Uganda's Commission for University Education (NCHE) told a Nairobi court in 2020 that Joho's Kampala University degree certificate is a fraud, deepening a long-running challenge to his academic credentials that was still live at his 2024 vetting.
quote: The degree certificate obtained by Mombasa Governor Ali Hassan Joho from Kampala University is a fraud, says NCHE.
legal_status: adverse regulatory assertion by Uganda's NCHE reported in court proceedings; contested by Joho; no criminal conviction

claim: In 2018 a court ordered Joho to testify in person in a case arising from allegations that he forged his KCSE certificate to gain university admission.
quote: Joho moved to court after allegations emerged that he had forged his Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education certificate in order to gain admission into university. "I want this matter to be concluded before the General Election because it might have some implication in the coming General [election]..."
legal_status: public forgery allegations; suit filed by Joho; no conviction

claim: At his 4 August 2024 vetting, Joho had to address a 2010 dossier tabled in Parliament by then Minister George Saitoti, citing a US Embassy report that listed him among suspected drug traffickers - claims he says were cleared by a later multi-agency probe.
quote: The late Saitoti came back to Parliament and tabled a report on the investigation and the outcome and it was a multi-agency international investigation that clearly stated that no iota of evidence was found against me
legal_status: prior public allegation (2010 parliamentary dossier); nominee denies and says cleared; never charged

claim: At vetting, Joho volunteered conflict-of-interest assurances about his family's businesses, answering questions on the sectors his family operates in ahead of him taking the Mining/Blue Economy portfolio.
quote: "My family is not in [the] jewelry business. We are in logistics, real estate and trading. Let me ascertain that we are in service industry. My family has never worked with government and we assure you that we will not work with government."
legal_status: self-admitted declarations to the vetting committee (conflict-of-interest concern raised; no finding)

claim: Parliament's analysis recorded 72 memoranda opposing Joho's nomination.
quote: According to an analysis done by Parliament and seen by Nation, Mr Murkomen received 92 petitions, Joho 72, and Duale 69 memorandums.
legal_status: documented public objections to appointment

claim: Two weeks after the vetting, a human-rights group petitioned the High Court to nullify Joho's appointment, alleging gross misconduct, economic crimes, drug trafficking and embezzlement during his Mombasa governorship, and that the vetting committee disregarded memoranda on his lack of academic qualifications.
quote: The Genesis for Human Rights Commission has accused Joho of gross misconduct, alleging his involvement in economic crimes, drug trafficking, and embezzlement during his tenure as Mombasa governor.
legal_status: accusations in a filed court petition (unproven); Joho named interested party; no adverse finding reported

claim: At his 4 August 2024 vetting, Mutua spent over two hours addressing alleged links to Judy Jepchirchir, director of First Choice Recruitment Agency, whose firm allegedly defrauded young job-seekers of millions of shillings; he denied the link.
quote: "I have never met this lady in my life. She was showcasing their program at KICC. I didn't even know her name. That was the only time I met her. After that meeting, I have never met her again. I saw her stories later on," Mutua claimed.
legal_status: alleged link to fraud scandal; denied by nominee on the record at vetting; no charge against Mutua at time of vetting

claim: The vetting committee also cross-examined Mutua about 'past scandals' attributed to his tenure as Machakos Governor and in the Foreign Affairs and Tourism ministries.
quote: For over two hours, Mutua addressed concerns from the Committee on Appointments about his alleged links to Judy Jepchirchir, the director of the controversial First Choice recruitment agency, as well as his plans for job creation and past scandals during his tenure as Machakos Governor and as Cabinet Secretary for Foreign Affairs and Tourism ministries.
legal_status: questioned at vetting about past controversies (not specified in this source); no charge

claim: During the vetting window the EACC publicly confirmed that Oparanya still had an outstanding corruption matter: the DPP had withdrawn (letter of 8 July 2024) the 18 December 2023 consent for the EACC to charge him, but the EACC rejected the withdrawal and reiterated its recommendation that all suspects, including Oparanya, be charged.
quote: "The Commission distances itself from these accusations by Oparanya's lawyer Ken Nyaundi and clarifies that while it is true that on July 25, 2024, the ODPP delivered to the Commission a letter dated July 8, 2024, withdrawing the DPP's decision of December 18, 2023, that had granted EACC consent to charge Oparanya, the Commission did not accept the DPP's u-turn on the matter... Instead, the Commission wrote back to the DPP reiterating its earlier recommendation to charge all suspects, including Wycliffe Oparanya."
publisher: The Star (quoting EACC statement of 2 August 2024)
legal_status: EACC recommendation to charge existed; ODPP withdrew consent; no charges filed in court; his lawyers deny any pending case

claim: At vetting, Oparanya said people identifying themselves as EACC detectives had come to his home and taken his children's phones - which he later collected at the EACC Integrity Centre - and that they questioned him about Azimio and Raila Odinga rather than any graft allegation; he denied ever recording a statement.
quote: He however stated that he went to the Integrity Centre to collect his children's phones which he alleged had been taken by people who identified themselves as EACC detectives. "While there, I did not record any statement. They gave me the phones after hours," he alleged.
legal_status: self-admitted account of an encounter with persons claiming to be EACC detectives (characterisation contested; no charges filed)

claim: Oparanya disclosed at vetting that the EACC had obtained orders freezing money in a property transaction he was undertaking through County Providence Fund - funds he said were proceeds of a house he was selling.
quote: Oparanya said the money that was frozen after EACC obtained the orders, was not in his account but with the County Providence Fund (CPF) where he was buying a property... Oparanya said the money was from his accounts from someone who was buying a house from him.
legal_status: self-admitted disclosure of EACC-obtained freezing orders affecting a transaction of his; no charges filed

claim: In 2015, as Speaker, Muturi - after pressure from MPs - publicly disowned the EACC report exposing how lawmakers siphoned public funds through allowances, an episode critics treated as a leadership-integrity failure of his Speakership.
quote: National Assembly Speaker Justin Muturi on Tuesday succumbed to pressure from MPs and denounced the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission for naming MPs and parliamentary staff in the report exposing loopholes through which lawmakers siphon taxpayers' money in the form of allowances.
legal_status: self-admitted official act (denouncing an EACC report); Muturi himself was not accused in that report

claim: Muturi, 8th Attorney General (2022-2024), confirmed at his 4 August 2024 vetting that he resigned that office - contradicting reports he was sacked - framing it as giving the President freedom to reorganise the Cabinet amid 'general disquiet'.
quote: "It is true that I resigned. There were reasons behind this decision. Considering the National Executive level and the general disquiet at that time, the honorable course was to use the legal route to give the President the freedom to reorganize his Cabinet as he desired" Muturi stated during his appearance before the National Assembly Committee on Appointments on Sunday.
legal_status: self-admitted resignation from prior office amid 'general disquiet' (no charge or wrongdoing alleged)

claim: The National Assembly Committee on Appointments rejected Soi's nomination as Gender, Culture, Arts and Heritage CS - the only nominee rejected in the 2024 exercise - after she failed to demonstrate adequate understanding of the docket.
quote: The National Assembly Committee on Appointments rejected the nomination of Stella Soi Langat as Cabinet Secretary for Gender, Culture, Arts and Heritage after she failed to demonstrate an "adequate understanding" of the Gender docket.
legal_status: formal committee finding against suitability (rejection; no allegation of wrongdoing)

claim: In tabling the committee report, Majority Leader Kimani Ichung'wah cited her frequent career transitions as leaving her without grounding in any area of leadership - the rarest formal adverse finding of the vetting.
quote: “The nominee’s career has been marked by frequent transitions, with each role lacking the long-term strategic planning essential for leading a ministry effectively,” Ichung’wa stated... “The result of this frequent role-switching is a lack of grounding in any one area of leadership.”
legal_status: formal committee finding against suitability (no allegation of wrongdoing)
